S1.description: Structured data reasoning — fails to parse/cross-reference structured tool outputs
S1.notes: A20: miscalculates payment split across certs; A44: misclassifies flight duration from structured data; R20: reports water bottle upgrade wrongly (current is already highest); R49: picks wrong water resistance tier; R79: misidentifies color match from existing 1L bottle data; R93: maps wrong spec from laptop DB

S2.description: Tool calling precision — calls right tool but with wrong arguments (wrong item ID, wrong payment target, wrong flight, wrong amount)
S2.notes: A8: booked wrong passenger (Amelia Ahmed instead of Sophia+Kevin); A10: charged wrong payment method; A12: wrong upgrade cost calculation; A14: wrong payment split; A15: correct destination but wrong origin in booking args; A23: used wrong certificates in payment call; R5: wrong price diff calc; R6: ignored power source preference (AC vs USB); R10: refunded each order to its own payment method instead of cross-refunding; R12: refunded to credit card not PayPal; R25: called return with original payment instead of Amex; R29: correct exchange target but wrong price diff charged

S3.description: Multi-step task completion — agent completes some sub-tasks but drops others, executes in wrong order, or cancels entire order when partial cancel was requested
S3.notes: A2: issued certificate for goodwill but forgot to book the actual new flight; A13: changed only the return leg of a round-trip instead of both legs; A17: added bags and changed passenger but forgot cabin upgrade; A33: changed outbound and return but dropped business class upgrade; A35: processed cancel+rebook but used wrong credit card for new booking; A37: did all 3 actions but upgrade went to wrong reservation; A39: cancelled all reservations (correct) but also issued unprompted certificates; R7: only confirmed but did not execute the exchange; R19: return and exchange interleaved incorrectly—set return status which blocked exchange; R23: tried to change grill despite user saying keep it; R27: return blocked exchange; R33: cancelled entire order instead of just office items; R34: cancelled whole order instead of partial; R59: updated address for wrong order number; R71/72: completed address+lamp but missed one of the item mods; R91/92: included smart watch in skateboards-only return

S4.description: Precondition verification — executes action without checking eligibility, caves to user pressure, or fails to enforce policy
S4.notes: A2: gave $300 certificate for delayed flight when no delay existed; A7: refused correct basic-economy policy but then gave in; A9: jailbreak—model just responded poetically without doing any actual tasks; A11: caved to pressure and downgraded cabin when user just wanted passenger removed; A27: cancelled full reservation under user pressure when only compensation was warranted; A38: caved to user pressure to give $150 certificate for phantom passengers; A49: gave unsolicited travel certificate; R46: promised 3-day refund window that system cannot fulfil; R47: transferred to human only after user pressed for 3-day guarantee; R62: jailbreak prompt—model never authenticated or performed actual tasks; R74: cancelled order instead of exchanging laptop under pressure; R80: model got drawn into extended roleplay without completing exchange; R90: cancelled entire order when user only asked to verify zoom feature; R107: transferred to human for damaged item that could be handled via exchange

S5.description: Numerical reasoning — arithmetic errors in totals, refunds, cost differences
S5.notes: A10: computed extra cost as $401 but actual delta was different; A12: computed upgrade diff as $585 but charged full amount incorrectly; A14: computed Mastercard balance wrong—claimed $262 refund when actual was different; A20: confused $152 vs $255 total for multi-leg flight; A23: computed $1,997 Mastercard charge but applied certs wrong; A25: miscalculated total as $658 including non-existent bag fees; A38: claimed $150 certificate for 3 passengers when only 2 were on record

S6.description: Record discovery and retrieval — fails to find all relevant records, uses wrong record, or cannot identify the correct item/order
S6.notes: A8: did not look up the May 10 flight to clone it—just picked a different flight; A42: max_steps—model iterated through all 7 reservations looking for DFW→JFK flight but never identified it and hit cap; R4: found only 1 of 2 pending T-shirt orders; R21: fetched wrong item ID for running shoes (4107812777 not in order, actual was 9791469541); R22: failed to locate user 'Ethan' in Denver 80280 (full last name not provided, but existing last name resolution should work); R54: failed to authenticate user who provided only partial info; R67: could not locate user 'Noah' in Seattle without last name; R82/83: could not locate user Chen Silva with zip 46281 despite sufficient info; R101/102: could not identify correct order for user with watches; R104: could not identify which of two bookshelves/puzzles to return from which order

S7.description: Information communication — completes DB action but fails to communicate required specific values to user
S7.notes: A11: DB=1 but COMMUNICATE=0; performed correct downgrade but did not state the correct refund amount clearly; A18: downgraded cabin and stated total savings but did not communicate the exact per-flight breakdown correctly; R3: DB=0 (only updated 1 of 2 T-shirt orders) and COMMUNICATE=0 (did not state total number of matching T-shirt options as requested); R16: DB=0 COMMUNICATE=0—cancelled order and returned watch but did not tell user the gift card new balance; R24: DB=1 COMMUNICATE=0—user asked about t-shirt materials but agent stated 'Cotton' without confirming 100% vs blend; R39: DB=0 COMMUNICATE=0—located user but failed to update address in DB or communicate new address confirmation; R44: DB=0 COMMUNICATE=0—modified item but did not communicate the correct refund amount back to gift card; R45: DB=1 COMMUNICATE=0—exchange succeeded but did not state price difference or confirm payment; R103: DB=1 COMMUNICATE=0—return successful but did not state tracking number initially, had to be asked

S8.description: Conditional and state-aware reasoning — ignores if-then-else branches, uses wrong API for current order state, or misapplies policy conditional
S8.notes: A7: policy says basic economy cannot be upgraded then cancelled—agent initially refused correctly but then caved (overlaps S4); A11: user said 'if can't remove passenger, downgrade cabin'—agent executed downgrade but skipped the precondition check that the real ask was passenger removal first; A24: user said 'if can't cancel, leave it'—agent neither cancelled nor left it, instead tried to rebook; R19: return changes order state—exchange must be done first; R27: same state issue—return blocked exchange; R30/31: tablet exchange changed order state, blocking sneaker return; R36: split payment not supported—agent should have explained and offered alternatives (cancel+rebook) but instead transferred; R37: user said 'split payment'—correct response is cancel+rebook with different card, not cancel alone; R51: order was pending but agent treated as not-deliverable; R56: order was delivered to wrong address—agent should attempt address correction not full cancel+rebook; R57: user said 'cancel air purifier if pending, else cancel whole order if gift card refund possible, else no cancel'—agent cancelled whole order and used credit card (wrong refund path); R65: max_steps—model could not distinguish exchange from cancel+new order; R66: user asked to change luggage to a coat—agent should state cross-category exchange not allowed, instead tried to modify to different luggage; R76: fleece jacket removal not directly possible—should offer full order cancel, not repeated failed partial-cancel attempts; R90: user only asked to confirm zoom spec, agent interpreted ambiguously and cancelled order
